summary:
An immutable reusable-workflow reference does not itself bind files checked out by the called job. The old closing-keywords receiver used unavailable github.job_workflow_sha; its empty ref selected default main. Native caller41404363354/job125142934886 referenced31632a60 but checked out6b71233d. Those revisions had identical rule bytes, so this finding claims no incorrect historical lint verdict. It establishes a future source-fidelity gap.

The prepared successor keeps the standalone and Kit lint jobs identical. Both explicitly pin the protected rule commit and SHA256, use the pinned checkout action, and verify its normalized ref/commit outputs, actual Git HEAD and rule bytes before the unchanged lint command. Empty/default-main checkout refuses even when default main happens to equal the pin. A different commit with identical rule bytes still refuses. Credential persistence remains disabled and the job retains contents-read-only permissions without untrusted PR checkout or a new credential path.

The maintained test runner executes the source-binding controls from a fresh depth-one checkout. The initial fixture incorrectly required historical Git objects and ran zero controls in CI; that failure is retained. The repaired fixture creates its own two commits from digest-checked rule bytes and rebinds only copied fixture operands. It separately asserts production pins and the unchanged historical lint command digest, and refuses remotes, alternates and extra fixture history. Tests qualify the operand/checkout/guard boundary; they do not emulate all hosted-provider behavior. Exact required CI, actual current-base caller checkout/readback, legitimate existing-PR recovery and complete27-repository inventory acceptance remain open in #5195. Source capture grants no native write, activation or wholeDelivery acceptance.
title: Pinned reusable workflow references require an independently bound transitive checkout
